note: Workspace imports resolve from the sync folder (WR-28's design note). The dispute over the finding's later dynamic-import consequence is settled for the validation's correction, the whole-text reading the build follows (ADR 0001 §6, Q-WR-16).

cases.title: relative and absolute static imports, plus a transitive import

files.f/a/lib.ts:
import { z } from "../c/z";
export const h = () => "lib:" + z;

given.source:
import { k } from "/f/b/util.ts";
export function main() { return k; }

cases.title: a dynamic import with the identical literal of a static import

given.source:
import { h } from "./helper";
export async function main() { const m = await import("./helper"); return [h, m.h]; }

cases.title: a dynamic import of an extensionless relative path, with no static rewrite trigger, is not fetched
cases.note: On Windmill the script cannot be deployed: the specifier stays in the build output, the dependency scan reads it as a package named '.', and bun install fails (WR-26), so the script gets a lock error and no version a run by path can select. Here the bundle fails on the unresolved ./helper.

given.source: export async function main() { return (await import("./helper")).h; }

cases.title: a static specifier that matches a substring of a different dynamic specifier
cases.note: The oracle settled it for the validation reading, which the build follows: the static rewrite turns the dynamic literal into ./nested/./helper.ts, which is then resolved from the folder. The catalogue's example reaches another folder (../other/./helper) by the same rule.

given.source:
import { h } from "./helper";
export async function main() { const m = await import("./nested/./helper"); return [h, m.h]; }

cases.title: dot segments are normalised and never go above the root

given.source:

export function main() { return x; }

cases.note: The reference normalises dot segments; that .. stops at the root is this build's reading (open question in the PR).

cases.title: export from is a static import to Bun 1.3.10's scanner, so it is rewritten too
cases.note: Part of Q-WR-13 for the pinned Bun: its scanner reports export … from as an import statement.

given.source:
export { x } from "./lib";
export function main() { return 1; }

cases.title: a script with a hashbang line is scanned and rewritten
cases.note: The .ts rewrite reads imports with Bun.Transpiler().scan, which accepts a hashbang line; scanImports would not. Which scanner Windmill's loader uses is an open question (Q-WR-13).
